title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.834643: branch-only fe_sub corrections paid from a metered account

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.834643 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's 0cd0ad73 (125.838547) with one change: the loops' three fe_sub (dx in loop A, dy in prod, u in pass 2) are branch-only, 5 instructions plus 3 when a < b, and loop A, prod and pass 2 return their borrow counts. A separate account A, funded by CORR = 1155/256 instructions per walk in the step price, pays 3 per borrow and must hold the round's worst case 9n before each round or the attack stops with failure, so the work bound stays deterministic; its 2^94-milli-unit seed per processor is a hard row. Step 69699/128 + 1155/256 + 25693/2^23 = 549.0382 instructions. The disclosed premise C bounds each site's trail-average borrow rate by 1/2 + pi0 (pi0 = 2^-10 for dx, 2^-11 for dy and u), half CORR's pads; under C, Bennett's supermartingale and Ville's inequality keep the early stop below 2^-120, and the DKW inequality bounds a bad table by 2^-43.58. A census on production secp256k1 under a rule declared before it ran supports C (proof.md 5.4). The declared run executes pass1, prod and pass2 against big-integer affine secp256k1 and loop A against big-integer dx with 0 mismatches, checks every returned borrow count, enters all 1,935 + 258 exit stubs, recomputes the census rule from census-corr.json and re-walks 4,096 steps of one census walk with the shipped census_corr.py. R = 2^26, kappa = 1.0001, h = 0.000048 and p0 = 0.3900482 are kept. Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): 0cd0ad73, 02cc35d7, 850e11fe, 886e6f54, a00774d8, c06f6691, 4ac17b66, 445f9a1c, cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 0a1c5772, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 01488655, 2bd168b5, daf2c741, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, b5de673a, 02feb284. Under H1 and C the recovery probability is at least 0.39000009 > 0.39 (failure rows < 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Exact ledger: W_ledger < 2^125.8346426 units; Markov ratio at most 0.0000478120 (exact, rounded up; the run's float ledger prints 0.0000478139) < 0.000048; certificate.py checks the claim and that 125.834642 fails, in exact arithmetic. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 256th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, and a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub, every returned borrow count checked), both copies of loop A and the arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed; the borrow-census rule recomputed from census-corr.json and 4,096 steps of one census walk re-walked by census_corr.py. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^23 concurrent walks.
